content: PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer implementation review and follow-up. The latest head adds 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests, with joint mode genuinely evaluating candidate pairs rather than greedily selecting the best first origin. Review verdict: algorithm architecture 8/10, correctness of two search modes 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10; overall promising but not production-ready. Strengths: deterministic surface sampler proportional to world-space area via barycentric coordinates; origin evaluation includes actual segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility and usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values; joint-pair mode checks every legal coarse pair, ranks by bitset union, then applies quality and contribution tie-breakers; shared coarse-to-fine engine uses 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, and separate fixed-first and joint branches; tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. Blockers: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because every non-floor object stores its entire AABB as an obstacle and candidates within 0.3 m are rejected, so any origin inside the AABB gets zero clearance and is rejected—this affects single-GLB room imports, combined room shell + furniture, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, and large models whose AABB contains empty navigable space; fix is actual geometry clearance (camera sphere/capsule does not intersect nearby triangles) via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast, with obstacle bounds per connected mesh or spatial cluster, plus a regression test with one imported object containing a room floor, walls, and empty interior. (2) Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports: every triangle is expanded to a JavaScript object with three independent Vec3 arrays, a normal array, IDs, and area; for 3 million triangles minimum packed geometry is ~144 MB (positions 108 MB + normals 36 MB), and the actual representation is several times larger, then structured-cloned into the worker via postMessage creating another enormous representation, and the BVH recursively sorts/slices JavaScript index arrays with millions of temporary three-element array allocations causing extreme GC pressure; expected to work on default graybox but likely to freeze, spike memory, or crash on heavy imported projects previously hitting multi-million-triangle limits; fix is compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals? Float32Array, meshRanges Uint32Array, transforms Float32Array), transfer ArrayBuffers into the worker rather than cloning nested objects, and for the BVH use three-mesh-bvh, a flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries, while avoiding expansion of indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle. (3) Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because the panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to the worker, so the worker keeps the expensive optimizer off the UI thread but not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, or structured cloning; on complex models the app may freeze before the worker reports first progress; fix is to move extraction into the worker or make it chunked and yield between meshes. (4) 'Apply to selected panorama pair' is conceptually wrong: UI allows optimized origins to be written directly into the two existing panorama references via updatePanoReference(primaryPanoId, { origin: originA }) and updatePanoReference(secondaryPanoId, { origin: originB }), but an existing panorama was rendered/generate

Audit disproved completion on two points: PR #23 remains conflicted remotely with rewritten history unpublished (GitHub reports CONFLICTING/DIRTY), and imported-floor filtering still accepts large props (a 6×6 floor plus a disconnected 3×3 tabletop returned all four triangles as legal floor triangles; current size thresholds cap at 8 m² and the test only covers a 1.4×1.4 tabletop). Everything else checked out: typecheck, build, 81 targeted optimizer/multi-origin/WebGL tests, the full 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer test, and real production-scene benchmark evidence. The substantive fix is an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism so ambiguous large horizontal surfaces are user-constrained instead of guessed, plus the auditor's large-top regression; publication will happen only after that revision passes and a fresh auditor cannot find a hole. The candidate remains unchanged and clean while the subagent finishes the disproof pass. The audit took longer than the normal test gate, likely because it independently inspected rebase semantics and benchmark evidence in addition to rerunning focused checks; no blocker or request for input surfaced. A follow-up code inspection surfaced a missing file path (src/engine/projectionCoverage/options.ts does not exist) and a CoverageOptimizerPanel that synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to the worker, so the worker keeps the expensive optimizer off the UI thread but not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, or structured cloning; on complex models the app may freeze before the worker reports first progress.

The coverage optimizer UI (CoverageOptimizerPanel) synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating or posting to the worker, so the expensive optimizer runs off the UI thread but scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning remain on the main thread and can freeze the app on complex models. A missing file path was also noted: src/engine/projectionCoverage/options.ts does not exist. The optimizer core (src/engine/projectionCoverage/index.ts and candidateGenerator.ts) exports projection coverage functions and candidate generation, including projectCandidateToFloor, isCandidatePositionValid, generateOriginCandidates, and localCandidateOffsets. Tests in tests/projectionCoverage.test.ts build a large packed scene (>100,000 triangles, <3,000,000 bytes), verify acceleration distanceToGeometry, resolve coverage options, and run both fixed-first and joint-pair optimization, asserting sample counts, candidate counts, reachable coverage >= combined coverage, finite origins, and minimum origin separation.

The CoverageOptimizerPanel now supports an optional explicit allowed-floor region to constrain optimizer origins when imported geometry contains large roofs, platforms, or prop tops that geometry alone cannot distinguish from floors. The feature adds an allowedFloorRegions field to CoverageSceneData and passes optional world-space bounds through extractCoverageScene into surfaceSampler and candidateGenerator, where normalizeAllowedFloorRegions validates and clones the bounds, triangleIntersectsAllowedFloorRegion tests triangle/region overlap for floor selection, and floorPointIsAllowed rejects candidate positions outside the regions. The UI adds a Restrict optimizer to an allowed floor region toggle plus X/Y/Z min/max number inputs, defaults the region to a 5m box around the capture origin at camera height, and passes [floorRegion] or undefined to extractCoverageScene. A new test builds an imported object with a low floor and a higher large top, extracts coverage with a tight allowed region, asserts only the floor triangles are retained and all candidates sit at the camera height, and the README/regression-audit docs were updated to describe the explicit-bounds fallback. One patch attempt failed because the expected README line was not found, so the docs update was applied through a separate patch.

Round two of the adversarial audit found one concrete hole: the allowed-floor controls (toggle plus X/Y/Z min/max inputs) remained editable during a running analysis, but edits did not cancel or invalidate the in-flight job, so a stale result could appear under newly displayed or invalid bounds. The fix disables the toggle and all six number fields while status === 'running', and adds a browser regression asserting the controls lock during the optimizer job and unlock afterward. The rebased branch was force-pushed with lease, PR #23 is MERGEABLE, local/remote heads match and are based on current origin/main, and lint, unit tests (including the 100k+ triangle integration test), build, and e2e coverage-optimizer tests all pass. The remaining gap is a UI/race condition, not a constraint or coverage correctness issue.

Round two of the adversarial audit identified a stale-result race: the coverage optimizer's allowed-floor controls (toggle plus X/Y/Z min/max inputs) remained editable during a running analysis, but edits did not cancel or invalidate the in-flight job, so a stale result could appear under newly displayed or invalid bounds. The fix disables the toggle and all six number fields while status === 'running', and adds a browser regression asserting the controls lock during the optimizer job and unlock afterward. The rebased branch was force-pushed with lease, PR #23 is MERGEABLE, local/remote heads match and are based on current origin/main, and lint, unit tests (including the 100k+ triangle integration test), build, and e2e coverage-optimizer tests all pass. The remaining gap is a UI/race condition, not a constraint or coverage correctness issue. Round three found two stale-state holes: editing bounds after a completed run leaves the old result and origin-apply actions visible, even if those origins are outside the newly displayed region; and changing the primary panorama does not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result, so the region remains centered on the previous panorama. The in-flight locking fix itself works. PR publication, ancestry, benchmark evidence, heavy integration test, worker/refinement constraints, docs, and verification remain sound. The subsequent patch centralizes result invalidation for every optimizer input and synchronizes only untouched default bounds to the active capture origin, preserving user-authored bounds.

Round four of the adversarial audit identified a final cancellation edge: stale extraction failures could bypass the analysis-identity check and overwrite a newer analysis state with `failed`. The fix adds the same identity check to the extraction catch path and a regression guard around that cancellation boundary. Prior rounds fixed the in-flight locking of coverage optimizer controls (toggle plus six number fields disabled while status === 'running'), centralized result invalidation for every optimizer input, and synchronized untouched default bounds to the active capture origin. Both round-three stale-state paths are fixed and published: completed results disappear immediately when any bound changes, and active panorama/capture inputs invalidate results while untouched default bounds recenter automatically. PR #23 is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with local and remote heads matching current origin/main. Verification remains intact: focused 100K+ triangle integration test, build, typecheck, WebGL, desktop/phone browser regression (coverage optimizer completes without overflowing the Reference drawer), and workflow verification all pass. The branch remains clean and unchanged during the round-four pass.
